questions.text: Explain why the Fe atoms in the bicycle frame react with the Cu2 ions.
questions.context:
Base your answers to questions 66 through 69 on the information below and on your knowledge of chemistry.
Stamping an identification number into the steel frame of a bicycle compresses the
crystal structure of the metal. If the number is filed off, there are scientific ways to reveal
the number.
One method is to apply aqueous copper(II) chloride to the number area. The Cu2 ions
react with some iron atoms in the steel frame, producing copper atoms that show the 
pattern of the number. The ionic equation below represents this reaction.
Fe(s)  Cu2(aq) →Fe2(aq)  Cu(s)
Another method is to apply hydrochloric acid to the number area. The acid reacts with
the iron, producing bubbles of hydrogen gas. The bubbles form faster where the metal was
compressed, so the number becomes visible. The equation below represents this reaction.
2HCl(aq)  Fe(s) →FeCl2(aq)  H2(g)
